all six global serialized-text replacements in the frozen order
record count, output filename count, and filename set for this witness

expected_detector.units: Two task/profile projections from two synthetic tasks and one profile; not the frozen 2436-projection population.
expected_detector.boundary: Supply input_raw_text and profile_values to the hand-case projection boundary. The production adapter is not implemented or invoked by this design seat. No CLI fixture option is assumed. Do not bypass or rebind pinned production inputs.
adapter_requirements: Expose actual emitted or planned records as task_id, output_ordinal, output_filename, projected_task.

Read actual filename and task object associations from implementation results. Never recompute a filename from an ordinal, sort by task_id, relabel IDs, or reconstruct task objects from the expected fixture.
Keep the expected_records literal independent of the implementation under test.
Return planned names and objects in memory; create no real config_files outputs.
expected_detector.comparison: Compare the complete ordered actual_records with fixture.expected_records, including both full task objects. Use fixture.expected_filename_to_task_id as an additional association check, not as a substitute for the ordered-record comparison.
scope_of_assertions: Exactly two records with ordinals [0, 1] and task IDs [1, 0].
Record 0 associates config_files/0.json with the full task object whose task_id is 1.
Record 1 associates config_files/1.json with the full task object whose task_id is 0.
expected_detector.why_counts_are_insufficient: Correct and mutant results both contain two files with exactly the same filename set {config_files/0.json, config_files/1.json}; only the filename-to-task-object association changes.
expected_detector.predicted_pristine_output: PASS r29_index_shuffled_ids_1_0: 2 ordered task/filename/object associations match
expected_detector.predicted_mutant_output: FAIL r29_index_shuffled_ids_1_0 record[0].output_filename: expected config_files/0.json; got config_files/1.json
expected_detector.predicted_restored_output: PASS r29_index_shuffled_ids_1_0: 2 ordered task/filename/object associations match
expected_detector.prediction_status: Hand-derived expectations, not observed command output.

future_probe_protocol: Retain the exact pristine implementation bytes in the probe seat's own isolated scratch directory and record their SHA256; do not mutate production, the pinned source, or sibling scratch.
Run one fixed bounded detector on the pristine bytes and capture actual command, stdout, stderr, and exit status. A failing or unevaluable baseline is INCONCLUSIVE, not a killed mutant.
Apply only the filename-expression mutation and record the mutated SHA256. Run the identical detector, fixture, and adapter; record actual output and status.

In a finally-style restoration step restore the retained exact pristine bytes, even if detection fails. Record restored SHA256, require it equals pristine SHA256, and run the identical bounded detector again.

Classify KILLED only for a passing pristine baseline, a mutation-specific filename-association failure, and a passing exact-byte-restored run. Classify SURVIVED for passing pristine/mutant/restored runs. Classify baseline/restoration failures, mutation nonapplication, or unrelated errors INCONCLUSIVE.

observed_execution.restoration: No target bytes were mutated. No mutation or restoration experiment is claimed.

limits: No production implementation has been selected, read, changed, or executed by this design seat.
The frozen corpus index-equals-ID forecast is not measured here; this synthetic permutation deliberately separates the concepts.
This witness does not establish complete mutation coverage, runtime file-write behavior, benchmark task validity, deployment behavior, or round admission.
Other defects such as sorted input, changed IDs, or changed replacement order are not additional assigned mutants.
